20261107-0237-canva-course-voice-01

Script

Good design is about why things sit where they are. Use the rule of thirds to place your focal point. Four principles hold every layout together: alignment, proximity, repetition and contrast. Limit yourself to two fonts and one clear size for each level. Start your palette with one main colour, one support colour and a neutral. For body text, aim for at least 4.5 to 1 contrast, so people can read it easily.

#2voicevoice-en-standardcommercial_ok: yes

Job

20261107-0238-canva-course-voice-01

Script

Practice makes skills. Each project follows the same steps: write a brief, set specifications, build, then check quality. Here is a bakery post, built in one minute of fast-forward. Notice the single headline, the one photo, and the clear call to action. Next, the same design in three sizes: square, portrait and story. Keep key text away from the top and bottom of a story. Save every finished file in a Practice folder. Your portfolio will come from these files.

#3voicevoice-en-standardcommercial_ok: yes

Job

20261107-0239-canva-course-voice-01

Script

Advanced features save time. Brand Kit stores a client's logo, colours and fonts in one place, so every new design uses them with one click. Keep a separate kit for each client. Magic Studio uses AI for design ideas, copy, images and background removal. Always check AI output yourself: facts, prices, licences and client rules. Bulk Create turns one design into many from a spreadsheet, which is useful for name badges or product cards.

#4voicevoice-en-standardcommercial_ok: yes

Job

20261107-0240-canva-course-voice-01

Script

Clients hire on proof, not on software lists. Choose six to eight strong pieces. For each one, write a short case study: the problem, your approach, the output, and the result. If a piece was practice work, say so. Never claim a result you cannot support. Your portfolio should fit on one page, with your promise, your selected work, your services, proof, and an easy way to contact you. Keep a PDF version ready.

#5voicevoice-en-standardcommercial_ok: yes

Job

20261107-0242-canva-course-voice-01

Script

Start your price from the income you need. Add your business costs, then divide by the hours you can actually bill. Not every working hour is paid, because selling and admin take time too. Here, 1,100 divided by 50 billable hours gives 22 per hour. That is a starting point. Then price by value. Offer three packages, and make the middle one the best value. For a new client, ask for a deposit before you start.
